inputs.original_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement is another warning that students and families are being made to bear the cost of a dispute between government and union leaders. The government should meet its obligations, but it must also uphold order and insist that education is not held hostage by threats of an indefinite nationwide strike. A responsible settlement matters; so does putting students’ future ahead of political pressure.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement should be understood as a warning about years of unresolved obligations, not simply as union leaders holding students hostage. Students and families are right to worry about disruption, but blaming workers for using their collective leverage shifts attention from the government’s failure to meet its commitments. A just settlement must protect students’ education and workers’ rights—and address the institutional neglect that keeps turning disputes into crises.
